It has variously been claimed to be of [[Macro-Jê languages|Macro-Jê]] or isolate affiliation. Guató is a [[VSO language]], has [[Agglutinative language|agglutination]], and has [[Ergative–absolutive alignment|ergative alignment]].{{Cite web |title=Guató - Indigenous Peoples in Brazil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/en/Povo:Guat%C3%B3 |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}} ==Classification== [[Terrence Kaufman]] (1990) provisionally classified Guató as a branch of the [[Macro-Jê languages]], as did [[Aryon Rodrigues]] (1999){{Cite book |url=https://ribeiro.wdfiles.com/local--files/temp%3A1/The_Amazonian_Languages__Cambridge_Language_Surveys.pdf|title=The Amazonian languages|date=1999|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-57021-3|editor-last=Dixon|editor-first=Robert M. W.|series=Cambridge language surveys|location=Cambridge, UK ; New York|editor-last2=Aĭkhenvalʹd|editor-first2=A. I︠U︡}} and Martins (2011),Martins, Andérbio Márcio Silva. 2011. ''[https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/9886 Uma avaliação da hipótese de relações genéticas entre o Guató e o tronco Macro-Jê]''. Doutorado em Linguística. Universidade de Brasília. but no evidence for this was found by Eduardo Ribeiro and Hein van der Voort (2010).{{Cite journal |last=Ribeiro |first=Eduardo Rivail |date=October 2010 |title=Nimuendajú was right: The inclusion of the jabutí language family in the Macro-Jê stock |url=https://repository.ubn.ru.nl/bitstream/handle/2066/86080/86080.pdf |journal=International Journal of American Linguistics |language=en |volume=76 |issue=4 |pages=517–570 |doi=10.1086/658056 |issn=0020-7071}} Andrey Nikulin (2020) excludes this possibility.{{Cite thesis |last=Nikulin |first=Andrey |title=Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo |date=2020 |publisher=Universidade de Brasília |url=https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/tese%3Anikulin-2020/Nikulin_2020_Proto-Macro-Je.pdf |place=Brasília}} == History == === Documentation === The Guató language is first documented in a number of wordlists, beginning with [[François-Louis Laporte, comte de Castelnau]]'s 1851 publication, and followed by others through 1959. The only substantial grammar of Guató was written by Adair Pimentel Palácio and published in 1984. === Language contact === Marcelo Jolkesky (2016) identifies lexical similarities with the [[Bororo languages|Bororo]], [[Tupi languages|Tupi]], and [[Karib languages|Karib]] language families, which, according to him, are due to contact.{{cite thesis|last=Jolkesky |first=Marcelo Pinho de Valhery |date=2016 |url=http://www.etnolinguistica.org/tese:jolkesky-2016-arqueoecolinguistica |title=Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas |type=Ph.D. dissertation |location=Brasília |publisher=University of Brasília |edition=2}} ==Geographical distribution== Today, the Guató mainly reside in Guató Indigenous Territory and Baía dos Guató Indigenous Territory. All residents speak only Portuguese, and the two remaining speakers live elsewhere.{{cite book |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783110419405/html |title=Amazonian Languages: Language Isolates. Volume I: Aikanã to Kandozi-Chapra |date=2023 |publisher=Walter de Gruyter |isbn=978-3-11-041940-5 |editor-last=Epps |editor-first=Patience |location=Berlin |doi=10.1515/9783110419405 |editor-last2=Michael |editor-first2=Lev}} Loukotka (1968) reported that as of 1964, in [[Mato Grosso do Sul]], Brazil, Guató was spoken on the banks of the [[Paraguay River]] and up the [[São Lourenço River (Mato Grosso)|São Lourenço River]], along the Bolivian border.{{Ethnologue25|gta|Guató}} It was also spoken at [[Uberaba Lake]] in [[Santa Cruz Department (Bolivia)|Santa Cruz Department]], Bolivia. ==Phonology== === Vowels === The Guató vowel system, like that of the Macro-Jê languages, collapses a three-way distinction of height in oral vowels to two in nasal vowels. language|agglutinative]], and has [[Ergative–absolutive alignment|ergative alignment]]. == Syntax == Guató is a [[VSO language]]. ==Vocabulary== For more extensive vocabulary lists of Guató by Palácio (1984){{Cite thesis |last=Palácio |first=Adair Pimentel |title=Guató: a língua dos índios canoeiros do rio Paraguai |degree=PhD |publisher=Universidade Estadual de Campinas |year=1984 |lang=pt
